explain.convey: perimeter (parimap) = total length of the boundary of a closed shape → start at a corner, go along every side, end back at that corner; triangle 4 cm, 5 cm, 6 cm → all three sides go into the sum

viewCaption.hi: Triangle ki teeno bhujayein khol ke ek seedhi line par rakhi hain: 4 cm, 5 cm aur 6 cm, ek ke baad ek. Ungli ka poora safar yahi line hai.

point.hi: Is triangle ki bhujayein 4 cm, 5 cm aur 6 cm hain. Ungli ek kone se har bhuja par chalakar wapas usi kone par lao. Ungli jitna chali, wahi parimap hai.
point.en: This triangle's sides are 4 cm, 5 cm and 6 cm. Run a finger from a corner along every side and bring it back to the same corner. How far the finger went is the perimeter.

pointAlt.hi: Socho is triangle ka kinaara ek dhaage se bana hai. Ek kone se dhaaga khol ke seedha kar do: 4 cm, phir 5 cm, phir 6 cm, sab ek line mein. Us seedhi line ki poori lambai hi parimap hai.
pointAlt.en: Picture this triangle's edge made of a thread. Open the thread at one corner and lay it straight: 4 cm, then 5 cm, then 6 cm, all in one line. The whole length of that straight line is the perimeter.

prompt.hi: Ungli kone se chal ke wapas usi kone tak kul kitne cm chali?
prompt.en: How many cm in all did your finger go, from the corner back to that same corner?

hindi.hi: Is triangle ke poore kinaare ki lambai kitne centimetre hai?

whyAlt.hi: 9 cm mein sirf do bhujayein judi hain, aur ungli abhi kone par wapas nahi aayi; teesri bhuja bhi kinaare mein aati hai, use bhi jodo.
whyAlt.en: 9 cm adds only two sides, and the finger is not back at the corner yet; the third side is on the edge too, so add it as well.

simpler.hi: Board par triangle ki har bhuja par uska naap likha hai. Ungli jin bhujaon se guzri, un sabke naap milakar socho.
simpler.en: On the board each side of the triangle has its measure written on it. Think of the measures of all the sides your finger passed, put together.

simpler.hi: Kinaara matlab shape ki bahar wali line. Ungli ek kone se chal ke har bhuja se guzarti hai, aur jis kone se chali thi wahin rukti hai.
simpler.en: The edge is the shape's outside line. A finger starting at a corner passes along every side and stops at the corner it started from.

explain.convey: any polygon (bahubhuj) → same rule: add every side, however many; hexagon = 6 sides → 6 lengths in the sum; regular hexagon with only one side labelled 5 cm → the unlabelled sides still belong to the boundary → still added

viewCaption.hi: Hexagon ki chhahon bhujayein ek line par lagi hain, har bhuja 5 cm ki. Jin bhujaon par label nahi tha, woh bhi is line mein hain.
viewCaption.en: All six sides of the hexagon sit on one line, each side 5 cm. The sides that had no label are on this line too.

point.hi: Yeh hexagon hai, chhah bhujaon wala. Sab bhujayein barabar hain, par label sirf ek par hai: 5 cm. Baaki par kuch likha nahi, phir bhi woh kinaare mein aati hain. Parimap mein har bhuja aati hai, likhi ho ya na ho.
point.en: This is a hexagon, a shape with six sides. All its sides are equal, but only one has a label: 5 cm. Nothing is written on the others, yet they are still part of the edge. Every side goes into the perimeter, labelled or not.

pointAlt.hi: Shahad ke chhatte ka ek khaana dekho: uski chhah bhujayein hoti hain, sab ek jaisi. Yahan ek bhuja par 5 cm likha hai, toh baaki paanch bhi 5 cm ki hain. Parimap ke liye chhahon bhujayein ginni hain, sirf likhi hui nahi.
pointAlt.en: Look at one cell of a honeycomb: it has six sides, all alike. Here one side says 5 cm, so the other five are 5 cm too. For the perimeter we count all six sides, not just the labelled one.

simpler.en: Take your finger once all round the hexagon's edge, adding each side's length as you go.

simpler.en: Look at the side next to the labelled one: it is just as long, and so is the one after it. The hexagon's whole edge is made of sides like these.

explain.convey: perimeter = AROUND the shape (a thread along the edge) → a length → cm, m, km; area (kshetrafal) = INSIDE (tiles covering the surface) → a different quantity; 6 cm by 4 cm rectangle → the edge goes 6, 4, 6, 4 → add them, never 6 × 4

point.en: Now look at this rectangle, 6 cm long and 4 cm wide. The perimeter is a thread running along the edge: first 6, then 4 down the side, then 6, then 4. The space inside is the area, a completely different thing.

pointAlt.hi: Is rectangle ko ek photo frame socho. Frame ki lakdi sirf kinaare par hoti hai, 6, 4, 6 aur 4; beech mein photo hoti hai. Lakdi ki poori lambai parimap hai, aur photo ki jagah area.

simpler.hi: Socho yeh rectangle ek khet hai: chaaron taraf ki baad parimap hai, aur andar ghaas wali jagah area. Baad naapne mein ghaas ka koi kaam nahi.
simpler.en: Picture this rectangle as a field: the fence all round it is the perimeter, and the grassy space inside is the area. Measuring the fence has nothing to do with the grass.

hindi.hi: {friendF} ne 10 × 4 = 40 cm kaha. 10 aur 4 cm bhujaon wale is card ka parimap kitna hai?
hindi.en: {friendF} said 10 × 4 = 40 cm. What is the perimeter of this card with sides of 10 and 4 cm?

reask.hi: 10 cm lambe, 4 cm chaude card ka sahi parimap kitne centimetre hai?
reask.en: What is the correct perimeter, in centimetres, of a card 10 cm long and 4 cm wide?

did.hi: 10 × 4 ki jagah card ki bhujayein jodkar galti pakdi
did.en: caught a mistake by adding the card's sides, not 10 × 4

viewCaption.hi: Card ki chaaron bhujayein line par hain: 10 cm, 4 cm, 10 cm, 4 cm. Is line mein sirf kinaara hai, card ke andar ka kuch nahi.
viewCaption.en: The card's four sides are on the line: 10 cm, 4 cm, 10 cm, 4 cm. This line holds only the edge, nothing from inside the card.

why.hi: kinaare mein do lambai aur do chaudai: 10 + 4 + 10 + 4 = 28 cm
why.en: the edge has two lengths and two breadths: 10 + 4 + 10 + 4 = 28 cm

whyAlt.hi: 10 × 4 se card ke andar ki jagah bharti hai, kinaara nahi; kinaara 10 wali do bhujaon aur 4 wali do bhujaon se banta hai.
whyAlt.en: 10 × 4 fills the inside of the card, not its edge; the edge is made of two 10 cm sides and two 4 cm sides.

why.hi: Tumne 10 aur 4 ek-ek baar jode; card ke kinaare par ghoomo, lambi bhuja do baar milti hai, chhoti bhi.
why.en: You added 10 and 4 once each; go round the card's edge and you meet the long side twice, the short one too.

simpler.hi: Board par card ki chaaron bhujayein dekho, chahe number sirf do par likha ho. Socho, 10 × 4 ki jagah inke saath kya karna hai.
simpler.en: Look at all four sides of the card on the board, even if only two carry a number. Think what to do with them in place of 10 × 4.

ladder.why: decide perimeter vs area from the situation: lace around vs cloth covering
error-spot: {friend} stops at 5 of 6 sides of an L-shape → find the left-out side and the true perimeter
six unequal edges in a real context (exhibition board tape) → every edge, once

remediation.move: named-corner walk instead of a list of numbers: start at P, name each side as its length goes into the sum (PQ, QR, … TP); the sum is done only when the walk is back at P

viewCaption.hi: Board par paanch kone wala khet hai.
viewCaption.en: The board shows a five-cornered field.

say.hi: Khet ke kisi ek kone par ungli rakho, aur har bhuja par rukkar uski lambai jodo. Jod tab poora, jab ungli wapas usi kone par ho.
say.en: Put a finger on any one corner of the field, and stop at each side to add its length. The sum is done when the finger is back at that same corner.

simpler.hi: Ek haath ki paanchon ungliyan khol lo, har bhuja ke liye ek. Har bhuja ki lambai jodte waqt ek ungli band karo; paanchon band ho jaayein, tab jod poora.
simpler.en: Open all five fingers of one hand, one for each side. Fold a finger as you add each side's length; when all five are folded, the sum is done.

sayAlt.hi: Khet ke jitne kone hain, utni hi bhujayein hain: paanch kone, paanch bhujayein. Jab tak paanchon ki lambai na jud jaaye, jod adhoora hai.
sayAlt.en: A field has as many sides as corners: five corners, five sides. Until all five lengths are added, the sum is not finished.

prompt.hi: Khet PQRST: PQ 8 m, QR 5 m, RS 7 m, ST 6 m, TP 3 m. Khet ka parimap kitne metre hai?
prompt.en: Field PQRST: PQ 8 m, QR 5 m, RS 7 m, ST 6 m, TP 3 m. How many metres is the field's perimeter?

reask.hi: 8 m, 5 m, 7 m, 6 m aur 3 m bhujaon wale khet PQRST ka parimap kitne metre hai?
reask.en: How many metres is the perimeter of field PQRST, with sides 8 m, 5 m, 7 m, 6 m and 3 m?

viewCaption.hi: Line par khet ki paanchon bhujayein usi kram mein hain jaise P se chalte hain: PQ, QR, RS, ST aur TP.
viewCaption.en: The line has the field's five sides in the order you walk them from P: PQ, QR, RS, ST and TP.

why.hi: P se wapas P tak paanchon bhujayein: 8 + 5 + 7 + 6 + 3 = 29 m
why.en: P back to P, all five sides: 8 + 5 + 7 + 6 + 3 = 29 m

whyAlt.hi: Tumhare jod mein khet ki ek bhuja chhoot gayi hai; P se chalkar board par woh bhuja dhoondo jiska number jod mein nahi aaya.
whyAlt.en: A side of the field has been left out of your sum; walk from P and find the side on the board whose number did not go into the sum.

answerViewCaption.hi: Khet ki paanchon bhujayein ek seedhi line mein hain: 8 m, 5 m, 7 m, 6 m aur 3 m. Poori line 29 m ki hai, yahi khet ka parimap hai.
answerViewCaption.en: The field's five sides are on one straight line: 8 m, 5 m, 7 m, 6 m and 3 m. The whole line is 29 m, the field's perimeter.

simpler.hi: Board par paanch naap likhe hain; jod mein paanchon number aane chahiye, ek bhi chhoote nahi.
simpler.en: Five lengths are written on the board; all five numbers must go into the sum, not one left out.

remediation.move: two numbers vs four sides, naming none of the then-card's numbers (the point before it already used a thread): the edge has four sides and the perimeter adds all four; length × breadth takes only two numbers and gives the little squares inside; the then-card asks what is left of a 150 cm ribbon

say.hi: Kinaare par chaar bhujayein hain, aur parimap chaaron ka jod hai. Lambai guna chaudai mein sirf do bhujayein aati hain; usse andar bichhe chhote square milte hain.
say.en: The edge has four sides, and the perimeter is the sum of all four. Length times breadth takes only two sides; it gives the little squares laid inside.

simpler.hi: Dhaaga kinaare par, chhote square andar. Humein dhaaga chahiye, toh chaaron bhujayein jodo.
simpler.en: Thread on the edge, little squares inside. We want the thread, so add the four sides.

sayAlt.hi: Is rectangle ko ek chhota aangan socho: deewar kinaare par chalti hai, aur andar farsh hai. Deewar ki lambai bhujaon se banti hai; lambai aur chaudai ka guna farsh par bichhe 1 m wale square ginta hai.
sayAlt.en: Think of this rectangle as a small courtyard: the wall runs along the edge, and inside is the floor. The wall's length is made of the sides; length times breadth counts the 1 m squares laid on the floor.

prompt.hi: 14 cm lambe, 9 cm chaude sticker ke kinaare-kinaare ribbon lagana hai. Tumhare 150 cm ribbon mein se kitna bachega?
prompt.en: Ribbon goes all along the edge of a sticker 14 cm long and 9 cm wide. How much of your 150 cm of ribbon is left?

reask.hi: 150 cm ribbon mein se 14 cm lambe, 9 cm chaude sticker ke kinaare-kinaare ek baar lagaane ke baad kitna ribbon bachega?
reask.en: Out of 150 cm of ribbon, how much is left after it goes once all along the edge of a sticker 14 cm long and 9 cm wide?

viewCaption.hi: Sticker ka kinaara line par khula hai: 14 cm, 9 cm, 14 cm, 9 cm. Ribbon isi line ke barabar lagega.
viewCaption.en: The sticker's edge is opened out on the line: 14 cm, 9 cm, 14 cm, 9 cm. The ribbon that goes on is as long as this line.

why.hi: kinaare par 14 + 9 + 14 + 9 = 46 cm lagega, toh 150 − 46 = 104 cm bachega
why.en: the edge takes 14 + 9 + 14 + 9 = 46 cm, so 150 − 46 = 104 cm is left

whyShort.en: the edge takes 46 cm, so 150 − 46 = 104 cm

whyAlt.hi: 24 cm tab bachta hai jab 150 mein se 14 × 9 ghatao; par ribbon sticker ke upar nahi bichhta, sirf kinaare par lagta hai: 14 wali bhuja do baar, 9 wali bhi do baar.
whyAlt.en: 24 cm is what is left when you take 14 × 9 from 150; but the ribbon is not spread over the sticker, it goes only along the edge: the 14 side twice, the 9 side twice too.

why.hi: Itna ribbon toh sticker ke kinaare par lag jaayega; sawaal yeh hai ki 150 cm mein se kitna bachega.
why.en: That much ribbon goes on the sticker's edge; the question is how much of the 150 cm is left over.

why.hi: Ismein lambi aur chhoti bhuja ek-ek baar hi ghati; ribbon 14 wali do aur 9 wali do bhujaon par lagta hai.
why.en: Here the long and the short side came off only once each; the ribbon goes on two 14 sides and two 9 sides.

simpler.hi: Sticker ke kinaare par ungli ek chakkar ghumao aur har bhuja ka naap jodo. Utna ribbon lagega; baaki 150 mein se bachega.
simpler.en: Take your finger once round the sticker's edge and add each side's length. That much ribbon goes on; the rest of the 150 is left.

bridgeToNext.hi: Seedhi bhujaon wali har shape mein har bhuja jodna chalta hai. Ab ek rectangle socho: iski bhujayein jodiyon mein aati hain, aur isse jodne ka ek jaldi wala tareeka milta hai.
bridgeToNext.en: For any shape with straight sides, adding every side works. Now think of a rectangle: its sides come in pairs, and that gives us a quicker way to add.

simpler.hi: Parimap kinaare ki saari bhujaon ka jod hai, andar ki jagah ka nahi. Ab rectangle ka parimap ek jaldi tareeke se nikaalenge.
simpler.en: Perimeter is the sum of all the sides on the edge, not of the space inside. Now we will find a rectangle's perimeter a quicker way.

covered.hi: Aaj dekha ki parimap band shape ke poore kinaare ki lambai hai: har bhuja ek baar, andar ki jagah nahi.
covered.en: Today we saw that perimeter is a closed shape's whole edge: every side once, never the space inside.

hook.convey: rectangle and square boundaries everywhere → their sides repeat → a quicker way than writing all four numbers each time

use.hi: Cricket pitch bhi ek rectangle hai. Uske kinaare ka hisaab lagane ka ek jaldi wala tareeka hai.
use.en: A cricket pitch is a rectangle too. There is a quick way to work out its edge.

use.hi: Ludo board ke kinaare ka hisaab ek jaldi tareeke se lagta hai. Pehle ek rectangle dekhte hain.
use.en: The edge of a ludo board can be worked out a quick way. First let's look at a rectangle.

explain.convey: rectangle (aayat) → opposite sides equal → going round: lambai, chaudai, lambai, chaudai; 10 m by 6 m → the board labels each length once, but the walk passes each twice

viewCaption.hi: Ek chakkar ki chaaron bhujayein ek line par hain: lambai, chaudai, phir wahi lambai aur chaudai dobara.
viewCaption.en: The four sides of one round are on one line: the length, the breadth, then the same length and breadth again.

point.hi: Is rectangle ki do lambi bhujayein 10 m ki hain, woh lambai hai. Do chhoti bhujayein 6 m ki, woh chaudai. Aamne-saamne ki bhujayein barabar hoti hain. 10 aur 6 ek-ek baar likhe hain, par chakkar lagao toh dono do-do baar milte hain.
point.en: This rectangle's two long sides are 10 m each: that is the length. The two short sides are 6 m: that is the breadth. Opposite sides are equal. 10 and 6 are written once, but go round and you meet each twice.

pointAlt.hi: Ek darwaaza socho: uski do lambi bhujayein ek jitni hain, aur do chhoti bhi ek jitni. Yahan bhi wahi baat hai: 10 m wali bhujayein do hain aur 6 m wali bhi do. Ek poora chakkar inhi chaar bhujaon se banta hai.
pointAlt.en: Think of a door: its two long sides match, and its two short sides match too. It is the same here: there are two 10 m sides and two 6 m sides. One full round is made of just these four sides.

prompt.hi: Ek poora chakkar kitne metre ka hua?
prompt.en: How many metres is one full round?

hindi.hi: Kone se ghoom kar wapas usi kone tak aane mein kitne metre lagenge?
hindi.en: How many metres does it take to go round from a corner back to the same corner?

reask.hi: 10 m lambe, 6 m chaude is rectangle ka ek poora chakkar kitne metre ka hai?
reask.en: How many metres is one full round of this rectangle, 10 m long and 6 m wide?

did.hi: rectangle ki lambai aur chaudai do-do baar ginkar chakkar nikala
did.en: counted a rectangle's length and breadth twice each to find one round

why.hi: 10 aur 6 dono do-do baar aate hain: 10 + 6 + 10 + 6 = 32 m
why.en: 10 and 6 both come twice: 10 + 6 + 10 + 6 = 32 m

whyShort.hi: 10 do baar, 6 bhi do baar: 32 m

whyAlt.hi: Rectangle mein 10 wali bhujayein do hain aur 6 wali bhi do; chakkar mein chaaron aati hain, sirf ek lambi aur ek chhoti nahi.
whyAlt.en: The rectangle has two 10 sides and two 6 sides; a round takes in all four, not just one long and one short.

why.hi: Tumne 10 ko 6 se guna kiya; woh rectangle ke andar ki jagah ka hisaab hai, chakkar toh kinaare par lagta hai.
why.en: You multiplied 10 by 6; that works out the space inside the rectangle, and a round goes along the edge.

simpler.hi: Ungli ek kone se ghumao: har mod par ek bhuja khatam hoti hai, aur chaar mod ke baad tum wahin pahunchte ho.
simpler.en: Run your finger round from one corner: each turn ends a side, and after four turns you are back where you began.

simpler.hi: Board par sirf do number likhe hain, par bhujayein chaar hain. Har likhi bhuja ke saamne uski jodidaar bhuja hai, bilkul utni hi lambi.
simpler.en: Only two numbers are written on the board, but there are four sides. Opposite each labelled side is its partner, exactly as long.

explain.convey: one length + one breadth = corner to the opposite corner = HALF the way round; the full round = that half twice → P = 2 × (l + b); on a new 12 m by 5 m rectangle the child does 2 × (12 + 5) = 34 m; l + b alone = 17 m = only half the boundary

viewCaption.hi: Is line ki pehli do bhujayein, 12 m aur 5 m, aadha chakkar hain. Baaki do bhujayein bilkul unhi jaisi hain.
viewCaption.en: The first two sides on this line, 12 m and 5 m, are half a round. The other two sides are exactly the same.

point.hi: Ek aur rectangle: 12 m lamba, 5 m chauda. Upar baayein kone se chalo, 12 m aage, phir 5 m neeche. Ab tum saamne wale kone par ho: aadha chakkar. Baaki aadha bhi utna hi lamba hai. Isliye parimap = 2 × (lambai + chaudai).
point.en: Another rectangle: 12 m long, 5 m wide. From the top-left corner go 12 m along, then 5 m down. Now you are at the opposite corner: half a round. The other half is as long. So perimeter = 2 × (length + breadth).

pointAlt.hi: Is rectangle ki chaar bhujaon ko do jodiyon mein baanto: ek 12 m aur ek 5 m ki jodi, aur waisi hi doosri jodi. Ek jodi ka jod lo aur uska do guna karo: yahi 2 × (lambai + chaudai) hai.
pointAlt.en: Split this rectangle's four sides into two pairs: one 12 m and one 5 m in a pair, and a second pair the same. Take one pair's sum and double it: that is 2 × (length + breadth).

prompt.hi: Is rectangle ke liye 2 × (lambai + chaudai) kitna banta hai?
prompt.en: For this rectangle, what does 2 × (length + breadth) come to?

reask.hi: Lambai 12 m, chaudai 5 m: 2 × (lambai + chaudai) kitna?
reask.en: Length 12 m, breadth 5 m: what is 2 × (length + breadth)?

hindi.hi: Is rectangle mein lambai aur chaudai jodo, phir 2 se guna karo: kitna aata hai?
hindi.en: In this rectangle add the length and the breadth, then multiply by 2: what do you get?

did.hi: 2 × (lambai + chaudai) se rectangle ka parimap nikala
did.en: used 2 × (length + breadth) to find a rectangle's perimeter

why.hi: aadha chakkar 12 + 5 = 17 m, aur uska do guna: 2 × 17 = 34 m
why.en: half a round is 12 + 5 = 17 m, and double that: 2 × 17 = 34 m

whyShort.hi: aadha chakkar 17 m, do guna 34 m
whyShort.en: half a round is 17 m, double is 34 m

whyAlt.hi: 17 m par tum sirf saamne wale kone tak pahunche ho; shuru wale kone tak lautne mein utna hi raasta aur lagta hai.
whyAlt.en: At 17 m you have only reached the opposite corner; getting back to the starting corner takes the same distance again.

why.hi: Tumne sirf 12 ka do guna karke 5 joda; bracket mein lambai aur chaudai dono hain, do guna poore bracket ka.
why.en: You doubled only the 12 and then added 5; the bracket holds both length and breadth, and the whole bracket is doubled.

simpler.hi: Formula mein bracket pehle: usmein lambai aur chaudai jaati hain. Phir bracket ka do guna.
simpler.en: In the formula the bracket comes first: the length and breadth go in it. Then twice the bracket.

simpler.hi: Ek kone se saamne wale kone tak do raaste hain, ek neeche se aur ek upar se. Dono mein ek lambai aur ek chaudai hai, isliye dono barabar, aur dono milke poora chakkar.
simpler.en: From a corner to the opposite one there are two ways: along the bottom or the top. Each takes one length and one breadth, so they are equal and together make the full round.

explain.convey: square (varg) → all 4 sides equal → side + side + side + side = 4 × side; the answer is a length → cm, not square cm; square of side 6 cm

viewCaption.hi: Is line mein square ki chaaron bhujayein ek jaisi lambi dikhti hain, har ek 6 cm.
viewCaption.en: On this line the square's four sides all look the same length, each 6 cm.

point.hi: Ab ek square lo: uski chaaron bhujayein barabar hoti hain, yahan har ek 6 cm. 6 ko chaar baar jodne se achha, seedha 4 × bhuja. Parimap ek doori hai, toh jawab centimetre mein aayega, square centimetre mein nahi.
point.en: Now take a square: its four sides are all equal; here each is 6 cm. Rather than adding 6 four times, just do 4 × side. A perimeter is a distance, so the answer comes in cm, not square cm.

pointAlt.hi: Square ko aisa rectangle maano jiski lambai bhi 6 cm hai aur chaudai bhi. Toh pichhla formula yahan bhi chalega: 2 × (6 + 6), wahi chaar bhujayein. Parimap ek doori hai, isliye jawab centimetre mein, square centimetre mein nahi.
pointAlt.en: Take the square as a rectangle with length 6 cm and breadth 6 cm too. The last formula works here as well: 2 × (6 + 6), the same four sides. A perimeter is a distance, so the answer is in centimetres, not square centimetres.

prompt.hi: Is square ka parimap kitna hai?
prompt.en: What is this square's perimeter?

reask.hi: Har bhuja 6 cm; is square ka parimap kitne cm?
reask.en: Each side is 6 cm; how many cm is this square's perimeter?

did.hi: square ki chaaron bhujaon ka kul naap nikala
did.en: found the total measure of a square's four sides

why.hi: chaar bhujayein, har ek 6 cm: 4 × 6 = 24 cm, parimap ek doori hai isliye cm
why.en: four sides of 6 cm: 4 × 6 = 24 cm, a perimeter is a distance, so cm

whyShort.hi: chaar bhujayein, har ek 6 cm: 4 × 6 = 24 cm

whyAlt.hi: 36 square ko andar se bharne wale chhote khaanon ki ginti hai; parimap mein sirf uski chaar bhujayein judti hain.
whyAlt.en: 36 counts the little boxes that fill the square inside; the perimeter adds only its four sides.

why.hi: Yeh square ki do hi bhujayein hain; kinaare par kone se ghoom kar wapas aao, har bhuja ek baar milti hai.
why.en: That is only two sides of the square; go round the edge from a corner and back, and you meet every side once.

why.hi: Ginti sahi hai, par parimap kinaare ki doori hai, jaise dhaage ki lambai; square wala naap andar ki jagah ka hota hai.
why.en: The count is right, but a perimeter is the distance round the edge, like a thread's length; a square measure is for the space inside.

simpler.hi: 6 cm ki chaar bhujaon ko ek seedhi line mein khol kar socho. Woh line kitni lambi hogi, wahi jawab hai.
simpler.en: Picture the four 6 cm sides opened out into one straight line. How long that line is, is the answer.

simpler.hi: Square mein ek bhuja jaan lo toh baaki teen bhi pata, kyunki sab barabar hain. Aur dhaage ko scale par naapte hain, isliye jawab centimetre mein aata hai, square centimetre mein nahi.
simpler.en: In a square, know one side and you know the other three, because they are all equal. And a thread is measured on a ruler, so the answer comes in centimetres, not square centimetres.

problem.hi: Ek notebook ka cover rectangle hai, 24 cm lamba aur 18 cm chauda. Uske kinaare par ek baar tape lagani hai.
problem.en: A notebook cover is a rectangle, 24 cm long and 18 cm wide. Tape goes once along its edge.

problemAlt.hi: Socho cover ke ek kone se tape chipkaana shuru kiya, aur kinaare-kinaare chalte hue wapas usi kone par pahunche. Roll se jitni tape khuli, wahi nikalni hai.
problemAlt.en: Picture starting the tape at one corner of the cover and going along the edge back to that same corner. However much tape came off the roll is what we find.

simpler.hi: Pehle ek chhota rectangle socho, 2 cm lamba aur 1 cm chauda, aur uske kinaare par ungli ghumao. Cover bhi aisa hi hai, bas uski bhujayein badi hain.
simpler.en: First picture a small rectangle, 2 cm long and 1 cm wide, and run a finger round its edge. The cover is just the same, only its sides are bigger.

givens.hi: lambai aur chaudai pata hai, dono centimetre mein
givens.en: the length and the breadth are known, both in cm

find.hi: cover ka parimap, utni hi tape lagegi
find.en: the cover's perimeter; that is how much tape

prompt.hi: Poore kinaare ki tape ke liye pehle 24 aur 18 ke saath kya karoge?
prompt.en: For tape round the edge, what do you first do with 24 and 18?

hindi.hi: Tape ka hisaab shuru karne ke liye 24 aur 18 ka kya karna hai?
hindi.en: To start working out the tape, what do we do with 24 and 18?

jod ka do guna karna hai

reask.hi: 24 cm lambe, 18 cm chaude cover ke kinaare par tape lagani hai. Tape ke hisaab mein pehle 24 aur 18 ka kya karoge?
reask.en: Tape goes along the edge of a cover 24 cm long and 18 cm wide. In working out the tape, what do you first do with 24 and 18?

told.hi: Pehle 24 aur 18 jodte hain, kyunki tape kinaare par chalti hai: ek lambai, phir uske bagal wali chaudai.
told.en: First we add 24 and 18, because the tape runs along the edge: one length, then the breadth beside it.

do.hi: Pehle dekho 24 aur 18 ka kya karna hai

why.hi: tape kinaare par chalti hai, ek lambai phir ek chaudai

simpler.hi: Tape cover ke andar nahi, kinaare par lagti hai: pehle ek lambi bhuja, phir uske bagal wali chhoti bhuja.
simpler.en: The tape goes on the cover's edge, not inside: first a long side, then the short side beside it.

told.hi: Toh 24 + 18 = 42 cm. Itni tape ek lambai aur ek chaudai par lagti hai.
told.en: So 24 + 18 = 42 cm. That much tape goes on one length and one breadth.

why.hi: itni tape ek lambai aur ek chaudai par lagti hai
why.en: that much tape goes on one length and one breadth

simpler.hi: 24 aur 18 ko upar-neeche likho, aur ikaai se shuru karke jodo.
simpler.en: Write 24 and 18 one under the other and add, starting with the ones.

viewCaption.hi: Cover ka poora kinaara ek line mein khula hai: lambai, chaudai, phir lambai, chaudai.
viewCaption.en: The cover's whole edge is opened into one line: length, breadth, then length, breadth.

prompt.hi: Tumhari baari: poore kinaare par kitni tape lagegi?
prompt.en: Your turn: how much tape goes on the whole edge?

reask.hi: Ek lambai aur ek chaudai par 42 cm tape lagti hai; poore kinaare par kitni lagegi?
reask.en: 42 cm of tape goes on one length and one breadth; how much goes on the whole edge?

did.hi: aadhe chakkar ka do guna karke poori tape nikali
did.en: doubled half a round to find the whole tape

simpler.hi: Cover ki tape kholo toh ek line banegi: 24, 18, phir dobara 24, 18. 42 cm us line ka pehla aadha hai.
simpler.en: Open the cover's tape out and it makes one line: 24, 18, then 24, 18 again. 42 cm is the first half of that line.

why.hi: poore chakkar mein do aadhe chakkar hain: 2 × 42 = 84 cm
why.en: a full round holds two half rounds: 2 × 42 = 84 cm

whyAlt.hi: 42 cm tape cover ka aadha chakkar hai, ek kone se saamne wale kone tak; wapas pahunchne ko utni hi tape aur chahiye.
whyAlt.en: 42 cm of tape is half a round of the cover, from one corner to the opposite one; getting back takes as much tape again.

answer.en: 84 cm of tape for the cover

why.hi: rectangle ke chakkar mein lambai aur chaudai do-do baar aati hain
why.en: round a rectangle, the length and the breadth each come twice

reask.hi: Rani 50 m lambe, 30 m chaude park ke teen chakkar daudti hai. Kul doori jodne se pehle kaunsi ek doori jaanni padegi?
reask.en: Rani runs three rounds of a park 50 m long and 30 m wide. Which one distance must we know before adding up the total?

told.hi: Pehle ek chakkar ki doori chahiye, kyunki teeno chakkar ek jaise hain. Rani kinaare par daudti hai, toh ek chakkar park ka parimap hai.
told.en: First we need one round's distance, because the three rounds are alike. Rani runs along the edge, so one round is the park's perimeter.

do.hi: Pehle ek chakkar ki doori chahiye
do.en: First we need one round's distance

why.hi: teeno chakkar ek jaise hain, aur Rani kinaare par daudti hai

simpler.hi: Rani har chakkar mein park ke poore kinaare par daudti hai, aur teeno baar wahi raasta hai. Socho, kaunsi doori teen baar judegi.
simpler.en: Each round Rani runs the park's whole edge, the same path all three times. Think which distance gets added three times.

told.hi: Ek chakkar mein Rani 50 m, 30 m, 50 m aur 30 m daudti hai. Teen chakkar mein yahi poori doori teen baar judegi.
told.en: In one round Rani runs 50 m, 30 m, 50 m and 30 m. In three rounds this whole distance adds up three times.

why.hi: teeno chakkar ek jaise hain

simpler.hi: Teeno chakkar ek hi raaste par hain, toh ek chakkar ki doori teen baar judegi.

prompt.hi: Tumhari baari: teen chakkar mein Rani kul kitne metre daudi?
prompt.en: Your turn: how many metres did Rani run in all in three rounds?

reask.hi: 50 m lambe, 30 m chaude park ke teen chakkar mein Rani kul kitne metre daudi?
reask.en: How many metres in all did Rani run in three rounds of a park 50 m long and 30 m wide?

did.hi: park ka ek chakkar nikaal kar Rani ke teen chakkar ki doori nikali
did.en: found one round of the park, then the distance of Rani's three rounds

simpler.hi: Pehle ek chakkar nikalo, yaani park ka parimap; phir socho, teen chakkar mein uska kya karna hai.
simpler.en: First find one round, the park's perimeter; then think what to do with it for three rounds.

why.hi: ek chakkar 2 × (50 + 30) = 160 m, aur teen chakkar 3 × 160 = 480 m
why.en: one round is 2 × (50 + 30) = 160 m, and three rounds 3 × 160 = 480 m

whyAlt.hi: 240 m tab aata hai jab ek chakkar mein lambai aur chaudai ek-ek baar gino; chakkar mein dono do-do baar aati hain.
whyAlt.en: 240 m comes from counting the length and the breadth once each in a round; in a round both come twice.

why.hi: Yeh ek chakkar ki doori hai; Rani ne aise teen chakkar daude the.
why.en: That is the distance of one round; Rani ran three such rounds.

viewCaption.hi: Yeh line Rani ka sirf ek chakkar hai: 50 m, 30 m, 50 m, 30 m.
viewCaption.en: This line is just one of Rani's rounds: 50 m, 30 m, 50 m, 30 m.

answer.en: 480 m in all for the three rounds

why.hi: park ka parimap 160 m hai, toh 3 × 160 = 480 m

prompt.hi: Ek square garden ke chaaron taraf kul 84 m baad lagi. Har bhuja par kitne metre baad lagi?
prompt.en: 84 m of fence went all round a square garden. How many metres of fence went on each side?

reask.hi: 84 m baad ek square garden ki chaaron barabar bhujaon par lagi; ek bhuja par kitne metre baad hai?
reask.en: 84 m of fence went on the four equal sides of a square garden; how many metres is on one side?

did.hi: 84 m baad ko square ki chaar barabar bhujaon mein baanta
did.en: shared 84 m of fence among a square's four equal sides

viewCaption.hi: Square garden ke neeche likha hai: baad 84 m, yaani poori baad. Uski chaaron bhujayein barabar hain.
viewCaption.en: Under the square garden it says: fence 84 m, the whole fence. Its four sides are equal.

why.hi: 84 m baad chaar barabar bhujaon par baanti gayi: 84 ÷ 4 = 21 m
why.en: 84 m of fence shared by four equal sides: 84 ÷ 4 = 21 m

whyAlt.hi: 42 m toh do bhujaon ki baad hai, yaani aadhi; square mein baad chaar bhujaon par lagi hai.
whyAlt.en: 42 m is the fence for two sides, only half; in a square the fence goes on four sides.

simpler.hi: Square ki saari bhujayein barabar hain, toh har bhuja par baad ka barabar tukda lagta hai.
simpler.en: All the sides of a square are equal, so each side takes an equal piece of the fence.

prompt.hi: Ek khet 30 m lamba aur 20 m chauda rectangle hai. Taar ₹15 per metre milti hai. Khet ke chaaron taraf ek baar taar lagane mein kitne rupaye lagenge?
prompt.en: A rectangular field is 30 m long and 20 m wide. Wire costs ₹15 per metre. How many rupees does it take to put wire once all round the field?

hindi.hi: 30 m aur 20 m wale khet ko poora gherne mein ₹15 per metre wali taar ka kitna daam lagega?
hindi.en: What will it cost to put ₹15-a-metre wire all round a 30 m by 20 m field?

reask.hi: 30 m lambe, 20 m chaude khet ke chaaron taraf ₹15 per metre wali taar lagane mein kitne rupaye lagenge?
reask.en: How many rupees does wire at ₹15 per metre take once round a field 30 m long and 20 m wide?

did.hi: pehle khet ka parimap joda, phir taar ka kharcha nikala
did.en: first added up the field's perimeter, then worked out the wire's cost

viewCaption.hi: Khet ka kinaara line par khula hai: 30 m, 20 m, 30 m, 20 m. Taar isi line jitni lambi lagegi.
viewCaption.en: The field's edge is opened out on the line: 30 m, 20 m, 30 m, 20 m. The wire is as long as this line.

why.hi: kinaara 2 × (30 + 20) = 100 m hai, aur 100 metre taar ka daam ₹1500
why.en: the edge is 2 × (30 + 20) = 100 m, and 100 metres of wire cost ₹1500

whyAlt.hi: ₹9000 tab aata hai jab 30 × 20 se andar ke 1 m wale square gin kar har square ke ₹15 lagao; taar zameen par nahi, kinaare par lagti hai.
whyAlt.en: ₹9000 comes from counting the 1 m squares inside with 30 × 20 and paying ₹15 for each; the wire goes on the edge, not on the ground.

why.hi: Yeh sirf aadhe chakkar ka daam hai, ek lambai aur ek chaudai; khet ke chaaron taraf lambai bhi do hain, chaudai bhi.
why.en: That is the price of only half a round, one length and one breadth; round the field there are two lengths and two breadths.

simpler.hi: Pehle aadha chakkar jodo, uski taar ka daam nikaalo, phir poore chakkar ke liye socho.
simpler.en: First add half a round, find the price of its wire, then think about the full round.

pictureCaption.hi: Dori ko seedha khol diya: pehle lambai, phir chaudai, phir lambai, phir chaudai. Chaudai wale dono tukdon par sawaal ka nishaan hai.
pictureCaption.en: The string is opened out straight: length, then breadth, then length, then breadth. Both breadth pieces carry a question mark.

prompt.hi: Ek 70 cm lambi dori ko mod ke rectangle banaya, aur poori dori kinaare mein lag gayi. Rectangle ki lambai 20 cm hai, toh chaudai kitne centimetre hogi?
prompt.en: A string 70 cm long was bent into a rectangle, and all of it went into the edge. The rectangle's length is 20 cm, so how many centimetres will its breadth be?

reask.hi: 70 cm ki poori dori se bane 20 cm lambe rectangle ki chaudai kitni hai?
reask.en: What is the breadth of a 20 cm long rectangle made from a whole 70 cm string?

did.hi: 70 cm ki dori se ulta chalkar rectangle ki chaudai nikali
did.en: worked back from a 70 cm string to the rectangle's breadth

viewCaption.hi: Dori mod ke yeh rectangle bana hai: poori dori 70 cm ki, aur ek bhuja par 20 cm likha hai.
viewCaption.en: The string is bent into this rectangle: the whole string is 70 cm, and one side says 20 cm.

why.hi: aadhi dori, 35 cm, mein ek lambai aur ek chaudai hai; lambai 20 cm hai, toh chaudai 15 cm
why.en: half the string, 35 cm, holds one length and one breadth; the length is 20 cm, so the breadth is 15 cm

whyShort.hi: aadhi dori 35 cm; lambai 20, toh chaudai 15 cm
whyShort.en: half the string is 35 cm; length 20, breadth 15

whyAlt.hi: 50 cm mein abhi ek lambai aur do chaudai hain, kyunki poori dori se ek hi lambai hatayi; lambai aadhi dori mein se hatao.
whyAlt.en: 50 cm still holds one length and two breadths, because only one length was taken from the whole string; take the length from half the string.

why.hi: 35 cm aadhi dori hai: lambai aur chaudai dono usmein judi hain; chaudai sirf uska ek tukda hai.
why.en: 35 cm is half the string: the length and the breadth are both joined in it; the breadth is only one piece of it.

simpler.hi: Dori ke chakkar mein lambai do baar aati hai aur chaudai do baar. Socho, aadhi dori mein kya-kya aata hai.
simpler.en: In the string's round the length comes twice and the breadth twice. Think what half the string holds.

ladder.why: backward for a square: perimeter 400 m → one side
backward for a rectangle: perimeter and length known → halve, then subtract the length
fencing cost: perimeter × ₹ per metre, then the gate variant → subtract 2 m before multiplying

remediation.move: the round run backward, naming none of the then-card's numbers and no operation: full boundary = 2 lengths + 2 breadths; the opposite corner = half a round = 1 length + 1 breadth; then the then-card's pond, given by its full round

say.hi: Socho, rectangle ke poore chakkar mein do lambai aur do chaudai hain. Kone se saamne wale kone tak sirf aadha chakkar hai: ek lambai aur ek chaudai.
say.en: Picture it: a rectangle's full round holds two lengths and two breadths. From a corner to the opposite corner is only half a round: one length and one breadth.

simpler.hi: Poore chakkar mein do lambai aur do chaudai hain. Aadhe mein bas ek-ek.
simpler.en: A full round has two lengths and two breadths. Half of it has just one of each.

sayAlt.hi: Chhoti sankhya par dekho: parimap 10 cm aur lambai 3 cm. 10 ka aadha 5 cm, yaani ek lambai aur ek chaudai; 5 mein se 3 gaye toh chaudai 2 cm. Jaanch: 3 + 2 + 3 + 2 = 10 cm.
sayAlt.en: Look at small numbers: perimeter 10 cm and length 3 cm. Half of 10 is 5 cm, one length and one breadth; 5 take away 3 leaves a breadth of 2 cm. Check: 3 + 2 + 3 + 2 = 10 cm.

viewCaption.hi: Yeh ek chhota rectangle hai: parimap 10 cm, aur ek bhuja 3 cm ki.
viewCaption.en: This is a small rectangle: the perimeter is 10 cm, and one side is 3 cm.

pictureCaption.hi: Talaab ka chakkar khol kar seedhi line bana di: lambai, chaudai, lambai, chaudai. Chaudai wale dono tukde abhi sawaal ke nishaan hain.
pictureCaption.en: The pond's round opened out into a straight line: length, breadth, length, breadth. Both breadth pieces are still question marks.

prompt.hi: Ek rectangle talaab ke kinaare ek poora chakkar 90 m ka hai. Talaab 28 m lamba hai. Woh kitna chauda hai?
prompt.en: One full round of the edge of a rectangular pond is 90 m. The pond is 28 m long. How wide is it?

reask.hi: Jis 28 m lambe talaab ka poora chakkar 90 m hai, woh kitna chauda hai?
reask.en: A pond 28 m long is 90 m all the way round; how wide is it?

viewCaption.hi: Talaab ki ek bhuja par 28 m likha hai, aur poore chakkar par 90 m.
viewCaption.en: One side of the pond says 28 m, and the full round says 90 m.

why.hi: ek lambai aur ek chaudai milkar 45 m hain, aur lambai 28 m, toh chaudai 17 m
why.en: one length and one breadth make 45 m together, and the length is 28 m, so the breadth is 17 m

whyShort.hi: lambai aur chaudai milkar 45 m; chaudai 17 m
whyShort.en: length and breadth make 45 m; breadth 17 m

whyAlt.hi: 62 m mein ek lambai aur dono chaudai bachi hain; poore chakkar se dono lambai hatao, phir jo bache uska aadha lo.
whyAlt.en: 62 m still holds one length and both breadths; take both lengths from the full round, then halve what is left.

simpler.hi: 90 m ka aadha karo, toh tum saamne wale kone par ho. Wahan tak ke raaste mein lambai ke baad jo bacha, wahi chaudai hai.
simpler.en: Halve the 90 m and you are at the opposite corner. On the way there, what is left after the length is the breadth.

remediation.move: wire is bought by the metre of edge, not by the ground inside: thread around the plot vs tiles inside it; cost = edge length (m) × ₹ per m; l × b = ground covered, not wire

say.hi: Plot ke kinaare par taar lagi hai. Lambai guna chaudai plot ki zameen naapta hai, taar nahi. Daam kinaare ke metre ka hai.
say.en: The wire runs round the plot's edge. Length times breadth measures the plot's ground, not the wire. The price is for the metres of edge.

simpler.hi: Socho taar kahan lagegi: plot ke beech mein ya uske kinaare par. Jahan lagegi, paise sirf wahi metre lete hain.
simpler.en: Think where the wire goes: across the middle of the plot or round its edge. Only the metres where it goes cost money.

sayAlt.hi: Dukaan par taar kapde ki tarah metre ke hisaab se bikti hai. Dukaandaar poochega kitne metre chahiye, zameen kitni badi hai yeh nahi; toh pehle kinaare ke metre jodo, phir har metre ka daam lagao.
sayAlt.en: At the shop wire is sold by the metre, like cloth. The shopkeeper asks how many metres you need, not how big the ground is; so add up the metres of edge first, then put the price on each metre.

prompt.hi: {friendM} ne 9 m lambe, 6 m chaude plot par ₹20 per metre wali taar ka kharcha ₹1080 bataya. Sahi kharcha kitna hai?
prompt.en: {friendM} said wire at ₹20 a metre round a plot 9 m long and 6 m wide costs ₹1080. What is the right cost?

reask.hi: 9 m lambe, 6 m chaude plot par ₹20 per metre wali taar ka kharcha ek dost ne ₹1080 bataya; sahi kharcha kitne rupaye hai?
reask.en: A friend put the cost of ₹20-a-metre wire for a plot 9 m long and 6 m wide at ₹1080; how many rupees is the right cost?

viewCaption.hi: Plot ki chaaron bhujayein ek line mein hain: 9 m, 6 m, 9 m, 6 m. Taar sirf isi line par lagti hai, andar ki zameen par nahi.
viewCaption.en: The plot's four sides are in one line: 9 m, 6 m, 9 m, 6 m. Wire goes only along this line, not on the ground inside.

whyAlt.hi: ₹1080 mein 9 × 6 = 54 ko ₹20 se guna kiya gaya hai; woh plot ki zameen ka hisaab hai, taar toh sirf kinaare ke metre par lagti hai.
whyAlt.en: ₹1080 multiplies 9 × 6 = 54 by ₹20; that works out the plot's ground, while the wire goes only on the metres of the edge.

why.hi: Tumne 9 aur 6 ek-ek baar jodkar daam lagaya; plot ke kinaare par 9 wali bhuja do hain, 6 wali bhi.
why.en: You added 9 and 6 once each and priced that; the plot's edge has two 9 m sides, and two 6 m sides.

simpler.hi: Pehle plot ka kinaara metre mein nikalo, phir har metre ka ₹20 lagao.
simpler.en: First find the plot's edge in metres, then put ₹20 on each metre.

covered.hi: Aakhir mein parimap se kaam liya: square ki bhuja, rectangle ki chaudai, chakkaron ki doori aur taar ka kharcha nikala.
covered.en: Last we put perimeter to work: a square's side, a rectangle's breadth, the distance of rounds, the cost of wire.

prompt.hi: Ek seedhe taar ko mod ke 27 cm lamba aur 9 cm chauda rectangle banana hai, bina kuch bachaaye. Taar kitne centimetre lambi honi chahiye?
prompt.en: A straight wire is bent into a rectangle 27 cm long and 9 cm wide, with none left over. How many centimetres long must the wire be?

did.hi: 27 cm aur 9 cm wale rectangle ki taar ki lambai nikali
did.en: found the wire length for a 27 cm by 9 cm rectangle

why.hi: Taar sirf kinaare par mudti hai: aadha chakkar 27 + 9 = 36 cm, aur poora chakkar 2 × 36 = 72 cm.
why.en: The wire only bends along the edge: half a round is 27 + 9 = 36 cm, and the full round 2 × 36 = 72 cm.

simpler.hi: Taar chaaron bhujaon par mudti hai: dono lambai aur dono chaudai.
simpler.en: The wire bends along all four sides: both lengths and both breadths.

reask.hi: 27 cm lamba, 9 cm chauda rectangle ek poori taar ko mod kar bana hai; woh taar kitne centimetre ki thi?
reask.en: A rectangle 27 cm long and 9 cm wide is made by bending a whole wire; how many centimetres was that wire?

covered.hi: Aaj dekha ki parimap band shape ke poore kinaare ka naap hai, jismein har bhuja ek baar judti hai. Rectangle ka parimap 2 × (lambai + chaudai), square ka 4 × bhuja, aur parimap se bhuja bhi nikaali.
covered.en: Today we saw that perimeter is the measure of a closed shape's whole edge, with every side added once. A rectangle's perimeter is 2 × (length + breadth), a square's 4 × side, and we also found a side from it.
